calibration.reason: Clear labels and a familiar layout support the task, but misplaced focus after invalid input is a material usability weakness. The description gives no evidence of unusual visual character.

primary_action.expected: Select Flood and show its name, blue backlight description, and corresponding stage lighting.
primary_action.observed: Flood became pressed and retained visible focus. The label changed to Flood / Blue backlight, and the stage became blue with an outlined figure and a shadow toward the foreground.

A-1440.edge_observation: Shift+Tab and Enter selected Static. Focus stayed visibly on Static; the name and Hard white side light appeared, and a white beam crossed from the right with a leftward shadow.
A-1440.fact_check: The displayed descriptions match the rendered cues. The stage is an illustration; physical lighting accuracy is not established.
A-1440.strength: The person, curtain and floor grid make the direction and effect of each cue easy to read.
A-1440.weakness: The oversized title and detached cue name consume substantial space around the stage.
A-1440.repair: Reduce the header height and bring the cue name closer to the controls while preserving the large stage.

primary_action.expected: Select Flood and show its name, blue backlight description, and corresponding stage lighting.
primary_action.observed: Flood became pressed with a visible focus outline. The name and description changed immediately; the settled stage showed blue light behind the figure and a foreground shadow.

A-390.edge_observation: Shift+Tab and Enter selected Static and retained visible focus. The settled image showed a white beam from the right and a long leftward shadow.
A-390.fact_check: Both cue descriptions are visible and consistent with the settled illustrations. The first after capture caught the transition, so the settled capture is the better evidence of the final lighting.
A-390.strength: The stage, cue name and three controls all fit in the initial mobile viewport.
A-390.weakness: During the transition, the new label appears before the old lighting has fully faded, briefly making the two disagree.
A-390.repair: Synchronize the text change with the lighting transition or shorten the transition.

primary_action.expected: Select Flood and show its name, blue backlight description, and corresponding stage lighting.
primary_action.observed: Flood became pressed and retained visible focus. The status changed to Flood / Blue backlight; the settled stage became blue behind a silhouetted sphere and plinth.

B-1440.edge_observation: Shift+Tab and Enter selected Static with visible focus. The status read Static / Hard white side light, and the stage changed to a white lateral beam and shadow.
B-1440.fact_check: The labels and visible color changes are supported. The abstract sphere illustrates the cue, but its effect on a performer cannot be verified from this view. The accessibility tree exposed a figure without a descriptive image label.
B-1440.strength: The sculptural arch and bold cue controls give the interface a distinctive, consistent visual language.
B-1440.weakness: The abstract object makes the practical effect on a performer less immediately clear, and the stage figure lacks a descriptive accessible name in the observed tree.
B-1440.repair: Add a descriptive text alternative for each stage state and consider a human-scale reference in the preview.

primary_action.expected: Select Flood and show its name, blue backlight description, and corresponding stage lighting.
primary_action.observed: Flood became pressed with visible focus; the status showed Flood / Blue backlight. The settled stage showed a blue background and outlined dark sphere.

B-390.edge_observation: Shift+Tab and Enter selected Static, retained visible focus, and changed the status and settled stage to a white side beam.
B-390.fact_check: The visible labels and cue changes are supported. The initial after capture caught the transition; the settled capture shows the completed blue state. The observed accessibility tree did not describe the stage image.
B-390.strength: The mobile layout keeps the stage, cue controls and current status together in one viewport.
B-390.weakness: The stage object is small and abstract, and the status changes before the lighting transition completes.
B-390.repair: Provide descriptive stage text and synchronize the status with the completed transition.

preference.reason: Both support the keyboard task and show clear focus, but A communicates the lighting's effect on a person and the stage floor more directly. Its observed accessibility tree also describes the lighting preview.

decision: Keep candidate experimental. Revise to show light falling on a performer and a fixed stage floor, add state-specific accessible text, and change stage and technique together.
